Group 1 (Case 1):
Here is the student’s answer for this case:
1. Case 1: Jugular foramen PEComa
The patient's hoarseness, dysphagia, vomiting, headache, and right CN IX–XII palsy localize to the skull base/jugular foramen. MRI shows a jugular foramen tumor with smooth rim enhancement and extrinsic compression; pathology confirms PEComa with HMB-45, Melan-A, and TFE3 positivity and S-100 negativity. These are definitive neoplastic findings. Normal coagulation, extrinsic compression rather than intrinsic thrombosis, and absent tuberous sclerosis history refute vascular/thrombotic, inflammatory/infectious, and genetic syndrome lesions. Thus the diagnosis is PEComa of the jugular foramen/skull base.

Here is the reference diagnosis for this case:
1. Case 1: Malignant perivascular epithelioid cell tumor (PEComa) of the jugular foramen
